title: fix(sim,motion,app): judge turning, rotary and 5-axis ball kinds on a reduced-fidelity model; the collision laws read its excess
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 3e9b8ae1, the merge of #911, which this work builds on).

## What changed

#864 / PR #911 flagged a STEP model imported coarser than promised, tightened the upright mill kinds' gouge laws by the model's excess, and refused every other kind outright. This PR takes three families off the refused list and makes the collision laws read the excess (the P1 raise from #911's review). The rule is #864's, unchanged: a tolerance gives the excess back while a positive tolerance is left (`verify::excess_floor`); past that the law reads untightened and the program gate refuses the operation by name. With no excess every law reads exactly as before.

**Now judged on a reduced-fidelity model**

| Family | Law that judges it | What reads the excess |
|---|---|---|
| Turning, band kinds (groove rough/finish, part, threading, form) | the meridian scan | its gouge clause (`turning::gouge_tol_on`; `blade_warnings_excess`, `thread_warnings_excess`, `form_warnings_excess`). The rest clause and the silhouette's chord budget keep the op's tolerance |
| A Part's inspection ask | the composed blade scan at the post | `blade_program_warnings_excess` |
| Turning, nose kinds (facing, profile, chamfer, taper, multi-pass, boring) | envelope law (f) | already tightened by #864; they were only refused |
| Every turning kind | meridian rapid, bar-feed and holder scans | their margin (`fidelity_law::tightened(GOUGE_TOL, excess)`) |
| Rotary contour / parallel / offset | law (f) and the radial field law | the field law's band and rapid allowances (`rotary_law::rotary_into`) |
| 5-axis contour and parallel, flow, multi-axis contour and rough | law (f) | nothing new: a posed ball is the same ball about the same centre, so (f) is the cut's whole gouge verdict |

**Collision laws in `verify` (all kinds)**

- (c) shank and holder reach, and its mid-turn sweep (c3): each band grows by the excess (`VerifyContext::band_growth`) and the kerf that excuses the flutes' own cut shrinks by it.
- (d) rapids in stock: the footprint's slack gives the excess back; the posed second reading gives it back out of the depth it lets a leaning stack stand in the part.

**The gate**

- The floor is per kind (`fidelity_law::floor_of`): the smallest of the 0.01 mm laws, the envelope tolerance, the meridian scan's tolerance and a Part's inspection ask. A groove held to 0.004 mm is refused on a metre-unit file while a 0.05 mm groove on the same file is judged.
- The setup's stock counts: an operation is judged with the worse of its source's and its stock's excess (`material::judged_material`, `model_fidelity::op_coarse`), because the collision laws read clearance against the stock.

**Still refused, each for a stated reason** (`fidelity_law`'s header): swarf and advanced swarf (the flank is proved clear only inside the generator; no verify law re-measures it), the cone and engrave rides, probe, the cross drill and plasma.

Structure only, to stay under the 400-line law: the blade judgments moved from `revolve.rs` to `turning/blade_law.rs`, the threading verdicts from `thread.rs` to `turning/thread_law.rs`, the excess readings from `verify/types.rs` to `verify/excess.rs`. The existing `*_warnings` functions keep their signatures and forward with an excess of 0.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/904-reduced-fidelity-laws.md`.

## How tested

Each pin holds a cut between the tightened and the plain tolerance (silent at full fidelity, convicted on the coarse model), a flush cut (never convicted by the tightening), a real gouge (convicted at every excess) and the reading past the bound (untightened).

- `camcraft-motion` `turning_coarse` (6 tests): blade, thread and form scans, the composed program scan, the rest clause, `gouge_tol_on`.
- `camcraft-sim` `coarse_collision` (5 tests): reach (c), sweep (c3), rapid (d) on a 90-gon boss whose chord error is the excess, the posed rapid reading, `band_growth`.
- `camcraft-sim` `model_excess::the_envelope_laws_gouge_half_answers_to_the_tolerance_less_the_excess`: law (f) in `Mode::Envelope` and `Mode::Rotary` (#904's point 6 for the envelope law).
- `camcraft-app` lib: `rotary_law::tests` (band and rapid allowances move by the excess), `turning_rapids::tests::the_margin_generation_hands_the_law_shrinks_with_a_coarse_models_excess`.
- `camcraft-app` `coarse_laws` (6 tests), through the document: a groove judged at 0.012 mm, refused by name at 0.030 mm, and the per-kind floor on a metre-unit file; a thread asked 0.046 mm too deep convicted only on the reduced model; a probe ask judged at the tightened budget and refused when the excess uses it up; a rotary contour judged, still convicting rapids through stock, refused past the bound; every kind in the registry either judged or refused for its reason; a stock copied from a coarser model.
- `camcraft-app` `coarse_contain`: the containment solid law on a drill run 0.008 mm past a blind floor, on a model flagged 0.0075 mm (#904's point 6 for that law).

Quick gate on the final head `10a31636`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` - sim, motion, app and ui suites, 4 steps, 0 failed (12.8 min; it runs every suite mapped to `sim::verify`, `motion::turning` and `app::operation::generate`, `model_fidelity` and the existing turning, rotary and rapid suites included). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- No document-level fixture for the turning margin or the rotary allowances: no generator emits a marginal graze on demand. They are pinned at the law with the value `generate` hands it.
- The multi-axis ball kinds are pinned by the registry test and by law (f)'s pin; no 5-axis operation was generated on a flagged model.
- The release tier (heavy lanes, UI snapshots) was not run.
- The excess is taken out along each law's own measure (a field ray, across a lean); on a surface oblique to that measure the mesh can stand further off than its chord error. Not corrected - noted in the decision record.

## Left open (filed)

- #1052 swarf's flank proof reads the excess (swarf stays refused until then).
- #1053 the cone and engrave rides, probe, the cross drill and plasma (with `rapids_radial`).
- #1054 the STEP facet budget as a setting (dialog, script verb, MCP `import_model`).
- #1055 metre-unit STEP scaled to millimetres before meshing.
- #1056 the flag gaps from #911's review (a stock copy after its source is deleted, older projects, the sim's gouge line near the refusal edge) and the display tolerances.
- #1057 **found while pinning, in the code #911 merged, not changed here:** a matched drill is convicted of a false gouge at its first plunge on a model flagged between about 0.0105 mm and the 0.015 mm bound. Law (b)'s 0.01 mm was sized to absorb our own regions' chord error and the excess takes it away. Safe side, but it blocks the post. The turning and rotary fixtures of this PR were run at 0.0105, 0.012, 0.0135 and 0.0149 mm and stay clean.

With these filed, everything #904 listed is either built here or has its own issue, so the umbrella can be closed when this merges.

Changelog: Turning, rotary and 5-axis ball operations are judged on a reduced-fidelity model with laws tightened by its excess (refused by name once nothing is left) instead of refused outright; shank/holder reach and rapid-in-stock checks read the excess too
Effort: max (not escalated)

Refs #904
